pages.text:
ORTEC advances AI-powered planning for more adaptive, resilient logistics operations.
ZOETERMEER, Netherlands, Oct. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ORTEC, a global leader in planning and decision-support software, today announced it has been mentioned as a Representative Vendor in the 2026 Gartner® Market Guide for Vehicle Routing and Scheduling (VRS). We hold the view that this recognition comes at a time when logistics organizations are facing growing operational complexity, increasing sustainability requirements and rising customer expectations, while simultaneously exploring how AI can improve planning, decision-making and execution.
For ORTEC, inclusion in the Market Guide underscores the company's continued investment in enabling organizations to move beyond traditional route optimization toward more intelligent, and adaptive logistics operations. As businesses seek solutions that can respond dynamically to disruptions, capacity constraints and changing delivery environments, ORTEC believes its combination of advanced optimization, logistics expertise and AI-powered decision support is uniquely positioned to help customers create lasting business value.
"We are proud to be recognized as a Representative Vendor in the 2026 Gartner Market Guide for Vehicle Routing and Scheduling," said Georgios Sarigiannidis, CEO of ORTEC. "We feel this reflects both the trust our customers place in us and the technology and expertise we have built over decades. Logistics operations are becoming increasingly complex. Organizations do not need more dashboards, alerts, or decisions. They need trusted systems that remove operational noise, automate what can be automated, and help people focus on what truly matters. By combining optimization, AI, and deep logistics expertise, ORTEC helps organizations build more resilient, efficient, and adaptable operations. We believe Gartner's recognition reinforces the direction we have chosen and the value we continue to deliver to customers every day".
Gartner defines a vehicle routing and scheduling (VRS) solution as "an application that creates vehicle routes and schedules, considering multiple constraints and service requirements while minimizing transportation fleet costs and mileage." Gartner's research notes that "The interest in VRS applications continues to grow, fueled by continued challenges resulting from supply chain disruptions, government regulations on emissions and expansion of various delivery models."
Among its key findings, Gartner reports that the influence of AI is being reflected in the VRS market: "AI is having a significant impact on VRS vendor roadmaps, transforming it from a feature enhancement into a core strategic mandate for future development," with most vendors already exploring AI agents and generative AI to support roles including dispatchers, planners, drivers, and customer support.
For our customers, partners, and prospective clients, we believe ORTEC's inclusion in the Market Guide reflects the company's expertise, market relevance, and commitment to AI driven innovation. In a rapidly evolving logistics landscape, organizations require partners they can rely on to navigate complexity, drive performance and embrace emerging technologies with confidence.
The 2026 Gartner Market Guide for Vehicle Routing and Scheduling is available on Gartner's website to Gartner subscribers.

We believe that it is one of the most important gatherings of CIOs and IT executives, the event brings together senior IT leaders to separate AI hype from reality, with agentic AI among this year's central themes. The network runs on directly licensed infrastructure, not resold capacity, across 90+ countries. Integrations with ElevenLabs, Retell AI, Vapi, Microsoft Teams, and Genesys let companies connect their existing AI solutions directly to DIDWW's network. Nutanix continues to expand its cloud native capabilities with the introduction of NKP Metal, extending NKP to provide unparalleled simplicity to Kubernetes deployments directly on bare-metal infrastructure. NKP Metal is designed to bring automated deployment, lifecycle management and enterprise data services to physical infrastructure, giving organizations greater flexibility to run modern and AI workloads across virtualized and bare-metal environments.

Gartner Inc (NYSE:IT), the research and advisory company, is expected to report third-quarter contract value growth of 2.5%, slightly above the 2.3% Visible Alpha estimate, according to UBS.
The analyst expects net new contract value to increase by $58 million in the quarter, down slightly from its previous estimate of $60 million.
Contract value growth excluding federal business is forecast to slow by about 40 basis points to 3.1% from 3.5% in the second quarter, reflecting a difficult renewal backdrop and selling environment.
UBS expects net new contract value excluding federal business of $45 million, down from its previous estimate of $60 million and last year’s $62 million.
Federal net new contract value is forecast at $13 million, compared with $11 million in the second quarter and a $49 million decline a year earlier, helped by seasonally higher government procurement in the third quarter.

Adjusted EBITDA guidance is expected to increase to at least $1.605 billion from $1.570 billion, while adjusted earnings per share guidance could rise to $14.55+ from $14.00+.

UBS trimmed its 2026 adjusted earnings per share estimate to $15.04 from $15.14, citing slightly lower fourth-quarter revenue from Conferences and foreign exchange.
For 2027, UBS cut its adjusted earnings per share estimate to $16.01 from $16.05 because of lower revenue, partly offset by a slightly higher margin and lower share count.

Gartner has identified four types of artificial intelligence it expects to reshape warehouse operations, ranging from established forecasting tools to robots that can perform physical tasks.
The research firm said warehouses have reached an inflection point for AI adoption. It pointed to persistent labor shortages, less risky ways to pay for automation, and the growing readiness of AI and autonomous technology for daily use.
Gartner’s framework weighs how independently a system can act and how sophisticated its intelligence is. The four categories cover software that predicts demand, generative AI that creates instructions, agents that help manage workflows, and robots that handle goods.
“These four AI trends are interconnected and reflect the evolution of a more intelligent, adaptive and resilient warehouse environment,” said Federica Stufano, senior principal analyst in Gartner’s Supply Chain practice. “As labor pressures persist and AI technologies mature, organizations are moving beyond experimentation toward operational deployment.”

Bedrock Data's approach to AI governance gives enterprises continuous, verifiable visibility into what every AI agent can access and real-time control over what it does with it
SAN MATEO, Calif., October 06, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Bedrock Data, the platform provider for DSPM, AI data security and governance, today announced it has been recognized in Gartner's Coolest Vendor Innovations in Data Security report. Bedrock Data's platform gives enterprises continuous visibility into data sensitivity, access, lineage and AI exposure across cloud, SaaS and on-premises environments at petabyte scale. Bedrock Data's AI Data Bill of Materials (DBOM) mentioned in the report, is a capability within ArgusAI, the company's AI security and governance product, as an innovation designed to strengthen governance, mitigate risk proactively and maintain security as AI adoption grows.
Security leaders are learning that AI risk extends across everything an agent, copilot or model can access in real time, as well as how that access is used when nobody's watching. Gartner projects that, "through 2028, 80% of unauthorized agentic AI transactions will be caused by internal enterprise policy violations, not cyberattacks, resulting in data corruption and operational liabilities."1 Bedrock Data found in its own telemetry that the median AI agent identity reaches 55 datastores, more than ten times what the median employee touches and nearly 8 in 10 of those identities can reach stored secrets like API keys and tokens. The Bedrock Data DBOM produces a defensible, continuously updated record of what data trains and feeds every AI system, without moving data outside customer boundaries, which is the foundation CISOs need before they can govern what happens next.
"There's no AI strategy without a data strategy. CISOs and CAIOs are being asked to manage AI risk without a record of what every agent, model and copilot can reach and how the underlying data or access change over time. Most have no way to produce one," said Bruno Kurtic, CEO and co-founder of Bedrock Data. "Our DBOM produces that record from our Metadata Lake and keeps it current, so governance rests on evidence instead of assumptions. We believe Gartner's recognition reflects what we hear from security leaders every day: they don't want to slow AI down, they want to prove it's safe."
Bedrock Data's ArgusAI: Bridging Data Governance and AI
Bedrock Data's ArgusAI gives technology and compliance leaders visibility into what AI systems can access, paired with the ability to control what happens next. Two capabilities anchor that product are its DBOM and Agent DLP capabilities.
Bedrock Data's DBOM gives technology and compliance leaders a way to move from assumed governance to verified governance. It automatically catalogs every dataset an AI system draws on for training, fine-tuning and inference. Built on Bedrock Data's Metadata Lake, Argus AI's DBOM produces an end-to-end, verifiable lineage record for every data source an AI system accesses, helping teams protect sensitive data before it ever reaches a model.
The capability is built into everyday workflows rather than delivered as a static report. Within the Bedrock Data interface, each datastore carries an interactive DBOM view covering sensitivity breakdowns, access history and entitlements, policy alignment such as encryption and retention, and full lineage and AI exposure tracing. DBOM also fingerprints data so lineage holds even as information is copied, transformed or reused across repositories, and it maps agent to data relationships to support guardrail gap analysis for organizations deploying AI agents.
Most recently, the company launched Agent DLP, a runtime data loss prevention capability built into ArgusAI, giving security teams not just visibility into what agents are accessing but lets them redact or block that access as it happens. Agent DLP sits inline at the agent gateway, inspects every tool call in both directions and enforces data access and regulatory policies in real time, extending ArgusAI from visibility into enforcement.
Bedrock Data has experienced rapid product expansion and company momentum recently. The company closed a $25 million Series A led by Greylock Partners and launched ArgusAI in late 2025 to extend governance into AI systems, followed by a strategic investment from Snowflake Ventures that included deeper technical integration with Snowflake's AI Data Cloud. ArgusAI was subsequently expanded to govern the enterprise AI risk surface, adding MCP Server Discovery and Snowflake Cortex governance alongside general availability of its MCP server.

The recognition follows the launch of Darwinbox Cortex, the AI-Native HCM platform, fundamentally reimagined with AI at its foundation rather than layered on top. Rebuilt from the ground up, Cortex defines a new category of HCM: moving beyond recording work to understanding, anticipating, and acting. "Darwinbox being one of only two vendors to score 3.4 or higher for Applied AI is meaningful validation of the direction we have taken with Cortex," said Chaitanya Peddi, Co-founder and Co-CEO, Darwinbox. "The next phase of AI in HR will not be defined by access to models alone. It will be defined by how deeply AI understands each organization: its people, roles, skills, policies, workflows, and permissions, and how reliably it can turn that understanding into action. Darwinbox's HCM Context Graph gives Cortex that foundation, enabling agents to reason and work across the employee lifecycle with the right governance and accountability. We believe the future of HCM is not merely a system that records how an organization works, but one that understands it and helps move work forward."
Gartner recognized Darwinbox's overall AI capabilities and strategy as a strength, highlighting the breadth of AI innovation across the platform, including more than 60 pre-built agentic and generative AI use cases, Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent2Agent (A2A) interoperability, and a no-code Agent Builder.
Cortex is the world's first HCM built on a Context Graph, a live, unified map of the organization: its people, roles, policies, workflows, and decisions. The Context Graph is what allows agents to reason across the full organizational context and act on it. For organizations, that means:
Everyone in HR becomes a builder.
HR teams describe what they need in plain language, and Cortex builds it, whether that is a process, a workflow or an agent. The Context Graph unifies organizational context, system capabilities and HR expertise, so AI reasons over live context rather than a static configuration.
Trusted autonomy, within set limits.
Agents reason and execute within an organization's existing permissions and governance. Every action is transparent, policy-aware, and accountable, leaving behind a receipt of every decision. That is how Cortex unlocks trusted autonomy that compounds, within the limits the organization sets.
Risks and opportunities surfaced early.
Cortex fundamentally changes how HR sees what is happening by continuously sensing patterns across roles, modules, and moments of the employee lifecycle that might otherwise remain hidden. It surfaces emerging risks and opportunities early, giving HR the ability to anticipate and act while outcomes can still be shaped.
Across organizations, Darwinbox AI is already changing how HR operates: understanding context, surfacing what matters earlier, and enabling HR to act at scale. At a full-service bank serving more than 18 million customers, time to hire fell from 33 days to 17 days, a 48% reduction, while HR queries dropped 31% year over year, with more than 43,000 interactions through Darwinbox AI.

pages.text:

Gartner expected to beat contract value estimates as UBS sees room for guidance upgrade
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 11:10 AM PDT 2 min read
Gartner expected to beat contract value estimates as UBS sees room for guidance upgrade Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock
Gartner Inc (NYSE:IT), the research and advisory company, is expected to report third-quarter contract value growth of 2.5%, slightly above the 2.3% Visible Alpha estimate, according to UBS.
The analyst expects net new contract value to increase by $58 million in the quarter, down slightly from its previous estimate of $60 million.
Contract value growth excluding federal business is forecast to slow by about 40 basis points to 3.1% from 3.5% in the second quarter, reflecting a difficult renewal backdrop and selling environment.
UBS expects net new contract value excluding federal business of $45 million, down from its previous estimate of $60 million and last year's $62 million.
Federal net new contract value is forecast at $13 million, compared with $11 million in the second quarter and a $49 million decline a year earlier, helped by seasonally higher government procurement in the third quarter.
UBS expects Gartner to raise its 2026 revenue guidance to at least $6.380 billion from $6.375 billion, although that would remain below the $6.395 billion analyst estimate.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance is expected to increase to at least $1.605 billion from $1.570 billion, while adjusted earnings per share guidance could rise to $14.55+ from $14.00+.
UBS expects the guidance increase to be driven primarily by margin contingency, while a $5 million increase in each of Conferences and Consulting would more than offset a $5 million foreign exchange headwind to Insights revenue.
The analyst models just under $200 million of share buybacks in the third quarter, noticeably below the levels of recent quarters, amid a potential moderation in repurchase activity.
UBS trimmed its 2026 adjusted earnings per share estimate to $15.04 from $15.14, citing slightly lower fourth-quarter revenue from Conferences and foreign exchange.
For 2027, UBS cut its adjusted earnings per share estimate to $16.01 from $16.05 because of lower revenue, partly offset by a slightly higher margin and lower share count.
UBS said indicators were mixed, with Gartner job openings about 10% below their mid-July peak, while the Business Roundtable CEO Index rose to 94.4 from 90.7 in the second quarter, its highest level since early 2022.

Gartner expected to beat contract value estimates as UBS sees room for guidance upgrade
Gartner Inc (NYSE:IT), the research and advisory company, is expected to report third-quarter contract value growth of 2.5%, slightly above the 2.3% Visible Alpha estimate, according to UBS.
The analyst expects net new contract value to increase by $58 million in the quarter, down slightly from its previous estimate of $60 million.
Contract value growth excluding federal business is forecast to slow by about 40 basis points to 3.1% from 3.5% in the second quarter, reflecting a difficult renewal backdrop and selling environment.
UBS expects net new contract value excluding federal business of $45 million, down from its previous estimate of $60 million and last year’s $62 million.
Federal net new contract value is forecast at $13 million, compared with $11 million in the second quarter and a $49 million decline a year earlier, helped by seasonally higher government procurement in the third quarter.
UBS expects Gartner to raise its 2026 revenue guidance to at least $6.380 billion from $6.375 billion, although that would remain below the $6.395 billion analyst estimate.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance is expected to increase to at least $1.605 billion from $1.570 billion, while adjusted earnings per share guidance could rise to $14.55+ from $14.00+.
UBS expects the guidance increase to be driven primarily by margin contingency, while a $5 million increase in each of Conferences and Consulting would more than offset a $5 million foreign exchange headwind to Insights revenue.
The analyst models just under $200 million of share buybacks in the third quarter, noticeably below the levels of recent quarters, amid a potential moderation in repurchase activity.
UBS trimmed its 2026 adjusted earnings per share estimate to $15.04 from $15.14, citing slightly lower fourth-quarter revenue from Conferences and foreign exchange.
For 2027, UBS cut its adjusted earnings per share estimate to $16.01 from $16.05 because of lower revenue, partly offset by a slightly higher margin and lower share count.
UBS said indicators were mixed, with Gartner job openings about 10% below their mid-July peak, while the Business Roundtable CEO Index rose to 94.4 from 90.7 in the second quarter, its highest level since early 2022.

SAN MATEO, Calif., October 06, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Bedrock Data, the platform provider for DSPM, AI data security and governance, today announced it has been recognized in Gartner's Coolest Vendor Innovations in Data Security report. Bedrock Data's platform gives enterprises continuous visibility into data sensitivity, access, lineage and AI exposure across cloud, SaaS and on-premises environments at petabyte scale. Bedrock Data's AI Data Bill of Materials (DBOM) mentioned in the report, is a capability within ArgusAI, the company's AI security and governance product, as an innovation designed to strengthen governance, mitigate risk proactively and maintain security as AI adoption grows.
Security leaders are learning that AI risk extends across everything an agent, copilot or model can access in real time, as well as how that access is used when nobody's watching. Gartner projects that, "through 2028, 80% of unauthorized agentic AI transactions will be caused by internal enterprise policy violations, not cyberattacks, resulting in data corruption and operational liabilities."1 Bedrock Data found in its own telemetry that the median AI agent identity reaches 55 datastores, more than ten times what the median employee touches and nearly 8 in 10 of those identities can reach stored secrets like API keys and tokens. The Bedrock Data DBOM produces a defensible, continuously updated record of what data trains and feeds every AI system, without moving data outside customer boundaries, which is the foundation CISOs need before they can govern what happens next.
"There's no AI strategy without a data strategy. CISOs and CAIOs are being asked to manage AI risk without a record of what every agent, model and copilot can reach and how the underlying data or access change over time. Most have no way to produce one," said Bruno Kurtic, CEO and co-founder of Bedrock Data. "Our DBOM produces that record from our Metadata Lake and keeps it current, so governance rests on evidence instead of assumptions. We believe Gartner's recognition reflects what we hear from security leaders every day: they don't want to slow AI down, they want to prove it's safe."
Bedrock Data's ArgusAI: Bridging Data Governance and AI
Bedrock Data's ArgusAI gives technology and compliance leaders visibility into what AI systems can access, paired with the ability to control what happens next. Two capabilities anchor that product are its DBOM and Agent DLP capabilities.
Bedrock Data's DBOM gives technology and compliance leaders a way to move from assumed governance to verified governance. It automatically catalogs every dataset an AI system draws on for training, fine-tuning and inference. Built on Bedrock Data's Metadata Lake, Argus AI's DBOM produces an end-to-end, verifiable lineage record for every data source an AI system accesses, helping teams protect sensitive data before it ever reaches a model.
The capability is built into everyday workflows rather than delivered as a static report. Within the Bedrock Data interface, each datastore carries an interactive DBOM view covering sensitivity breakdowns, access history and entitlements, policy alignment such as encryption and retention, and full lineage and AI exposure tracing. DBOM also fingerprints data so lineage holds even as information is copied, transformed or reused across repositories, and it maps agent to data relationships to support guardrail gap analysis for organizations deploying AI agents.
Most recently, the company launched Agent DLP, a runtime data loss prevention capability built into ArgusAI, giving security teams not just visibility into what agents are accessing but lets them redact or block that access as it happens. Agent DLP sits inline at the agent gateway, inspects every tool call in both directions and enforces data access and regulatory policies in real time, extending ArgusAI from visibility into enforcement.
Bedrock Data has experienced rapid product expansion and company momentum recently. The company closed a $25 million Series A led by Greylock Partners and launched ArgusAI in late 2025 to extend governance into AI systems, followed by a strategic investment from Snowflake Ventures that included deeper technical integration with Snowflake's AI Data Cloud. ArgusAI was subsequently expanded to govern the enterprise AI risk surface, adding MCP Server Discovery and Snowflake Cortex governance alongside general availability of its MCP server.

Gartner Inc (NYSE:IT), the research and advisory company, is expected to report third-quarter contract value growth of 2.5%, slightly above the 2.3% Visible Alpha estimate, according to UBS.
The analyst expects net new contract value to increase by $58 million in the quarter, down slightly from its previous estimate of $60 million.
Contract value growth excluding federal business is forecast to slow by about 40 basis points to 3.1% from 3.5% in the second quarter, reflecting a difficult renewal backdrop and selling environment.
UBS expects net new contract value excluding federal business of $45 million, down from its previous estimate of $60 million and last year's $62 million.
Federal net new contract value is forecast at $13 million, compared with $11 million in the second quarter and a $49 million decline a year earlier, helped by seasonally higher government procurement in the third quarter.
UBS expects Gartner to raise its 2026 revenue guidance to at least $6.380 billion from $6.375 billion, although that would remain below the $6.395 billion analyst estimate.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance is expected to increase to at least $1.605 billion from $1.570 billion, while adjusted earnings per share guidance could rise to $14.55+ from $14.00+.
UBS expects the guidance increase to be driven primarily by margin contingency, while a $5 million increase in each of Conferences and Consulting would more than offset a $5 million foreign exchange headwind to Insights revenue.
The analyst models just under $200 million of share buybacks in the third quarter, noticeably below the levels of recent quarters, amid a potential moderation in repurchase activity.
UBS trimmed its 2026 adjusted earnings per share estimate to $15.04 from $15.14, citing slightly lower fourth-quarter revenue from Conferences and foreign exchange.
For 2027, UBS cut its adjusted earnings per share estimate to $16.01 from $16.05 because of lower revenue, partly offset by a slightly higher margin and lower share count.

Certain financial measures used in this Press Release are not defined by U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”) and as such are considered non-GAAP financial measures. We provide these measures to enhance the user’s overall understanding of the Company’s current financial performance and the Company’s prospects for the future. Investors are cautioned that these non-GAAP financial measures may not be defined in the same manner by other companies and, as a result, may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures used by other companies. Also, these non-GAAP financial measures should not be construed as alternatives, or superior, to other measures determined in accordance with GAAP. The non-GAAP financial measures used in this Press Release are defined below.
Adjusted Revenues: Represents GAAP revenues less revenues from our Digital Markets divested operation. We believe Adjusted Revenues is an important measure of our recurring operations as it provides a more accurate period-over period comparison of trends in revenues.
Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin: Represents GAAP net income (loss) adjusted for: (i) interest expense, net; (ii) tax provision (benefit); (iii) gain on event cancellation insurance claims, as applicable; (iv) other (income) expense, net; (v) stock-based compensation expense; (vi) depreciation, amortization, and accretion; (vii) goodwill impairment and other asset impairments, as applicable, (viii) workforce reduction expenses and certain other non-recurring items and (ix) gain/loss on divestitures, as applicable. Adjusted EBITDA Margin represents Adjusted EBITDA divided by GAAP Revenue. We believe Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin are important measures of our recurring operations as they exclude items not representative of our core operating results.
Adjusted EBITDA Excluding Divested Operation and Adjusted EBITDA Margin Excluding Divested Operation: Represents Adjusted EBITDA as defined above less EBITDA from our Digital Markets divested operation. Adjusted EBITDA Margin Excluding Divested Operation represents Adjusted EBITDA Excluding Divested Operation divided by Adjusted Revenue. We believe Adjusted EBITDA Excluding Divested Operation and Adjusted EBITDA Margin Excluding Divested Operation are important measures of our recurring operations as it provides a more accurate and consistent period-over period comparison of our results.
Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS: Represents GAAP net income (loss) and diluted net income (loss) per share adjusted for the impact of certain items directly related to acquisitions and other non-recurring items. These adjustments include (on a per share basis, in the case of Adjusted EPS): (i) the amortization of acquired intangibles*; (ii) workforce reduction expenses and other non-recurring items; (iii) gain on event cancellation insurance claims, as applicable; (iv) the non-cash (gain) loss on de-designated interest rate swaps, as applicable; (v) goodwill impairment and other asset impairments, as applicable, (vi) gain/loss on divestitures, as applicable. and (vii) the related tax impact. We believe Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS are important measures of our recurring operations as they exclude items that may not be indicative of our core operating results.
* The Company excludes amortization of acquired intangibles because it is generally a fixed non-cash expense that can be significantly impacted by the timing and/or size of acquisitions and management does not use it to evaluate core operating results. Although the Company excludes the amortization of acquired intangibles from Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS, management believes that it is important for investors to understand that such intangible assets were recorded as part of acquisition accounting and contribute to revenue generation.
Free Cash Flow: Represents cash provided by operating activities determined in accordance with GAAP less payments for capital expenditures. We believe Free Cash Flow is an important measure of the recurring cash generated by the Company’s core operations that may be available to be used to repay debt obligations, repurchase our stock, invest in future growth through new business development activities, or make acquisitions.
Foreign Currency Neutral (FX Neutral): We provide foreign currency neutral dollar amounts and percentages for our contract values, revenues, certain expenses, and other metrics. These foreign currency neutral dollar amounts and percentages eliminate the effects of exchange rate fluctuations and thus provide a more accurate and meaningful trend in the underlying data being measured. We calculate foreign currency neutral dollar amounts by converting the underlying amounts in local currency for different periods into U.S. dollars by applying the same foreign exchange rates to all periods presented.
